[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1> and the camera holds completely still for the entire clip, keeping the exact viewpoint, framing, crop, subject scale, and placement of the reference image. <Subject 1> keeps the exact appearance established in <Picture 1> in every visible respect, and no feature, marking, covering, or accessory is introduced that is not already present there. <Subject 2> keeps the complete visible area exactly as referenced, including its surfaces, tonal transitions, gradients, shadows, lighting direction, and depth. <Subject 1> is never lifted out of the supplied scene and placed into a newly generated one, and the surroundings are never exchanged for a different setting. {"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS FOR THIS WORKFLOW

This is the ref2va model, which is a different model file from the first frame and text to video workflows. The settings were measured on this model, not copied across.

PICK ONE FROM THE DROPDOWN

CombinationSteadinessGrainTimeNotes
euler + simple5.2114.5128sThe default here.
res_multistep + simple5.1814.9228sTied with it. Nothing separates them.
euler + sgm_uniform5.3614.5328sFine.
euler + beta5.5614.6628sFine.
dpmpp_sde_gpu + sgm_uniform7.5014.5838sDo not use here. It zooms in and crops the frame instead of keeping the reference framing, and it is slower.


NEVER USE ddim_uniform

It does not just look worse, it replaces the scene. In testing on this exact workflow the background turned into a wall of sweet packet graphics and the cream onesie became a blue cartoon jumper. The character and the room, which are the whole point of this workflow, were gone.

The same thing happened on the first frame and the text to video models. Three different models, the same result.

Worth knowing: its steadiness score was 7.01, better than a pairing that actually works. A single number would have ranked the disaster higher. What exposed it was the grain figure (23.76 against 14.5) and looking at the frames.


WHY 4 STEPS IS ENOUGH HERE

The other workflows use 8 steps, because at 4 steps the generated sound is worse (found by blind listening, confirmed twice). Here the sound is yours, locked in by the Audio Sync node, so that reason disappears. The picture measured the same at 4 and 8, so 4 steps is the right choice and saves 10 seconds a clip.

The Dropdown has an 8 step option if you want to compare on a particular shot.


OTHER SETTINGS

Shift 6 and 3 on the node feeding the sampler. Leave them.

Audio fade is 0 and should stay 0. The fade exists to hide a click that the model puts at the start of sound it generates itself. Your track is supplied, so there is no click to hide, and a fade would just quietly alter your audio.

Control after generate under the seed: set it to fixed once you find a take you like, or the seed moves on the next run and you cannot get it back.
